name: Saifuddin Nasution Ismail
_note: M2 cohort expansion (key figures): Minister of Home Affairs since the unity government formed (3 Dec 2022). Objective spine plus a provisional Layer B pass on file; below ranking validity pending remaining objective dimensions and an independent Layer B panel. Layer B (Editorial Panel) is a SINGLE-CODER provisional first-coder pass (coderScores length 1): each score is recorded and cited but NOT scored, normalized, or ranked, per methodology.validity.minCodersToScore=3. Citations verified to exist via search; article full text was not opened (environment fetch restriction), so facts rest on cross-outlet-corroborated search summaries and require primary-source reconfirmation before any independent panel finalizes the score.

metrics.justification: No personal corruption charge or conviction of record. The one adverse personal court matter is a CIVIL defamation judgment (Alor Setar High Court, 24 Aug 2025, RM670,000 plus an apology, under appeal) arising from 2023 election-campaign statements about another politician — a civil matter from political speech, not an integrity or anti-corruption matter. Disclosed as context only; not recorded against the subject's integrity status.

citation.title: Court awards Sanusi RM670,000 in defamation case, orders Saifuddin Nasution to apologise

metrics.justification: Shapley-Shubik power index of the leader's coalition (Pakatan Harapan) among the seven blocs of the 222-seat Dewan Rakyat (GE15, simple-majority quota 112), computed by scripts/compute-pivotality.mjs. PH=0.4048, PN=BN=0.2214, GPS=0.0714. Coalition-level because per-party tallies carry a 1-2 seat contradiction immaterial to the index. Descriptive structural weight, not a merit score.

metrics.justification: Public-order handling of the KK Mart "Allah socks" episode and two molotov attacks on stores (late Mar 2024): said police were "out in full force" and urged those behind a boycott call to defuse the situation. A firm enforcement posture, but the crisis cooled over weeks rather than via a single decisive resolution (anchor 2).

citation.title: After second KK Supermart attack, home minister urges those behind boycott call to defuse situation

metrics.justification: Mixed reform delivery: the citizenship-equality Constitution (Amendment) Act (gazetted as Act A1752, royal assent 7 Mar 2025) was delivered, granting citizenship to overseas-born children of Malaysian mothers; the IPCC police-oversight body was stood up (commissioners named 10 Jan 2024) but materially diluted versus the IPCMC long demanded. One major reform gazetted, one diluted (anchor 3).

citation.title: Citizenship law amendments passed in Parliament with more than two-thirds majority

metrics.justification: The citizenship amendments secured Conference of Rulers consent (announced 19 Jul 2024) and a near-unanimous cross-bench Dewan Rakyat vote (206 of 207) on 17 Oct 2024 after consultation with MPs and all chief whips. A documented cross-bench instrument on a constitutional matter, though civil-society consensus was not reached (anchor 3).

citation.title: Amendments to citizenship law consented by Conference of Rulers, minister says

metrics.justification: After backlash he withdrew two regressive clauses from the citizenship bill (foundlings / abandoned children), announced 21 Mar 2024, stating the decision followed "intensive discussions" and feedback from MPs, legal experts and chief whips. A position reversed and explained on the record rather than dropped silently (anchor 3).

citation.title: Saifuddin Nasution: Let there be no more mention of foundlings denied citizenship
